# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 88 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 88 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_088_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 5

**1** Then the shepherd came and said to the virgins, "Have you done him any injury?" "Ask him," they said. I said to him, "Lord, I was very happy to remain with them." **2** "What did you eat?" he asked. "Lord," I said, "I ate the words of the Lord the whole night." **3** "Did they treat you well?" he asked. "Yes, Lord," I answered. **4** The shepherd smiled and said to me, "Do you know the name of the tall man?" "No," I said. "It is the Son of God," he answered. **5** "And why does he appear as a tall man?" I asked. "Because," he said, "he is taller than the tower." **6** "Well then, Lord," I said, "tell me also about the gate." "Listen," he said: "this gate is the Son of God; this is the only entrance to the Lord. No one shall enter in to him except through his Son. **7** You saw the six men and the glorious and great angel in the middle of them? He is the Son of God, and the six are the glorious angels who support him on the right and on the left. **8** Of these glorious angels, not one enters the presence of God without him; whoever does not take his name upon him shall not enter the kingdom of God." **9** "But what is the tower?" I asked. "The tower," he said, "is the church." **10** "And these virgins — who are they?" "They are holy spirits, and no man can otherwise be found in the kingdom of God unless these have clothed him with their garment; for if you take only the name and do not receive the garment from these, you will not profit." **11** "And the white garments of the virgins — what are they?" "They are their names," he answered; "if anyone who bears the name of the Son of God bears also all these names, he shall enter the kingdom of God."

---

*EMET: this chapter is the explicit key to the entire allegory. Rock = Son of God; gate = Son of God; tower = church. The dual requirement: the name (baptism) + the garment (virtues) = entry.*
